clue.text: Posturing that's risen in the past year

indicators.note: in a down clue something that has risen is read from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: something that happened in the past happened some time ago
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone notes that showing off has become more common over the last twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: AGO then Y, read upwards, gives YOGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga practice consists largely of holding bodily postures, so it can be playfully called posturing.

clue.text: Musical takes mikes off

indicators.note: something that has gone off is spoilt or out of order, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage show has its microphones removed before the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiss Me, Kate is the Cole Porter musical based on The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter's Broadway show of 1948 is a famous stage musical, so the generic word fits as an example.

clue.text: Wonderful place by a commercial university

blocks.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' in dimensions such as three by four
the indefinite article in its other form
a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
U is the usual abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A lovely spot stands next to a university that runs on business lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Using 'by' for X is a common crossword trick from the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu, Kubla Khan's summer capital in Coleridge's poem, stands for any idyllic, magnificent spot of splendour.

clue.text: Strengthen fort rented without any closing time?

indicators.note: each word is to go without the T, for time, that ends it

blocks.note: a redoubt is a small fortification
property that is rented has been let

explanation.surface: A garrison is reinforced, the rented fort apparently having no locking-up hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'any' tells you both pieces lose a final T: REDOUB plus LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To redouble an effort is to intensify or increase it greatly, making it stronger.

clue.text: Big Apple guy providing employment

blocks.note: first meaning: Steve ..., the major figure at Apple computers
second meaning: paid positions of work

explanation.surface: A New Yorker is creating work for people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Apple suggests New York, but here it is the big Apple company that Steve Jobs co-founded.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs are paid positions, and employment in the general sense means paid work held by people.

clue.text: Wayward teen filmed corruption

indicators.note: a wayward thing strays from its proper course, so these letters wander into another order

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebellious adolescent was caught on camera behaving corruptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Defilement is the act of making something impure or morally tainted, which is a form of debasement.

clue.text: Case of nobody born in Michigan?

blocks.note: read as 'no' person, so nobody gives NO
MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan
someone born in a place is a native of it

explanation.surface: A puzzling legal or medical case in which no one was born in Michigan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nobody born in Michigan' is 'no MI native'; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the nominative is the case of a noun that is the subject of a verb.

clue.text: Annoyance when splitting subtle distinction without first being worked on

indicators.note: the phrase is to lose its opening letter
something splitting a phrase goes into the middle of it, breaking it apart

blocks.note: a fine line is a subtle distinction between two things
'it gives me the pip' means it annoys me; the pip is a British word for irritation

explanation.surface: Someone gets irritated when a hair-splitting argument starts without its first point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pip' is British slang for irritation, as in 'it gives me the pip'; 'when' is just a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the pipeline is in progress, already under way and not yet finished or delivered.

clue.text: Regularly skip double gym to follow instruction

indicators.note: skipping at regular intervals means missing every other letter and keeping the rest

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are kept

explanation.surface: A fitness fan routinely misses a twice-weekly gym session, against orders.
explanation.walkthrough: Skip the odd letters of dOuBlE gYm.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey is to do as one is told, carrying out an order or command.

clue.text: Perhaps Domino's Pizza's major ingredients?

blocks.note: first meaning: ... Domino, the American rock and roll pianist, whose nickname is an example
second meaning: the greasy components that make up much of a pizza, such as cheese and oil

explanation.surface: Asks what goes into a pizza from the Domino's chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Domino's is a pizza delivery chain, but the apostrophe-s belongs to the clue: Domino is the musician Fats Domino.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese, oil and fatty meat are dietary fats, which make up much of a pizza; Fats was Domino's nickname.

clue.text: Having written something, in French, to the Thunderer's fashionable ...

blocks.note: au is French for 'to the'
Thor is the Norse god of thunder, so the Thunderer's is THOR'S
hip means trendy

explanation.surface: A writer sends a smart piece in French to The Times, nicknamed the Thunderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunderer is also a nickname of The Times newspaper, which the surface leans on; here it is the god Thor.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorship is the state or fact of being the writer of a book or other work.

clue.text: ... for Parisians, who study peace

blocks.note: qui is French for 'who'
an étude is a musical study

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: Parisians who read and learn in tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry the French theme on from 11 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Quietude is a literary word for stillness and calm, a state of tranquillity.

clue.text: Arab cult is working with small amount of silica

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and rearranged

blocks.note: eight of the letters to be rearranged
the last two letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious sect is employed alongside a little quartz-like mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double duty only in appearance; all of 'Arab cult is' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists call igneous rocks ultrabasic when their silicon dioxide content is very low, under about 45 per cent.

clue.text: Lulu, who has a strong voice

blocks.note: first meaning: a lulu is an outstanding example of something
second meaning: a singer who belts songs out

explanation.surface: Lulu, the Scottish pop singer, is described as a powerful vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish singer famed for the big-voiced 'Shout', which makes the surface seem a single description.
explanation.definitionFit: Both informal nouns mean a remarkable specimen, and a singer who belts songs out loudly is called that too.

clue.text: Learner driver tricks those who help motorists parking and help dogs

blocks.note: a learner driver displays L plates
to have someone is to fool them
the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British breakdown service
P is the sign for parking
SOS is the distress call asking for help

explanation.surface: A learner fools the breakdown crew, then the parking attendants come to help.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, whose patrols rescue broken-down drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa apsos are a small long-haired Tibetan breed, so the plural names several such animals.

clue.text: Change to new symbols, having read up on gender identity?

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one thing on another places it after, so the reading piece goes second

blocks.note: trans is short for transgender, a gender identity
someone who has read up on a subject is literate in it

explanation.surface: Someone who has studied gender identity can turn their text into another script.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'trans-literate': well read on gender identity.
explanation.definitionFit: To transliterate is to write words in the characters of a different alphabet or writing system.

clue.text: Rotting fodder that's stored across Italian river

indicators.note: a thing lying across another spans it, holding it within

blocks.note: silage is green fodder kept in a silo
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Cattle feed kept in storage has been carted over an Italian waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotting' works as a noun here, the process of decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoilage is the decay of food or produce, the process of going bad.

clue.text: Mother approved pushing ring back, to cope with limited means

indicators.note: the round letter shaped like a ring is shunted from the front to the back

blocks.note: an informal word for mother
OK'd, given the OK

explanation.surface: Mum gave the go-ahead to hocking a ring, to get by when money is tight.
explanation.walkthrough: The O at the front of OKED moves to the end, giving KEDO.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to manage with whatever is available, however inadequate.

clue.text: More than one bent on loss of head is captivating

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a bent is a penchant, an inclination, so more than one is the plural

explanation.surface: Several people bent on beheading someone make for a gripping story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' is a noun here, a liking.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchants is the verb form meaning charms or delights, just as captivating does after 'is'.

clue.text: Persuasive, firm, polite fellow

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: A description of a convincing, steady, courteous man.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is clear, logical and convincing, so it wins people over.

clue.text: Broken in halves, no good for vampire hunter

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Something snapped in two is useless to someone stalking vampires.
explanation.definitionFit: Professor Abraham Van Helsing is the doctor who pursues Count Dracula in Bram Stoker's novel.

clue.text: Joint of meat for 23

definitions.note: the answer to 23 across, a verb

blocks.note: first meaning: a knuckle cut of pork or ham
second meaning: to pledge goods for a loan

explanation.definitionFit: A hock is the joint above an animal's hoof, sold as a cut, and to hock goods is to leave them with a pawnbroker.

clue.text: Name on hand tool

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it

blocks.note: paw is an informal word for a hand
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone writes their name on their hand as an implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is someone used by others for their own ends, a person treated as a mere instrument.

clue.text: Hear complaint, say 22

indicators.note: hearing the word rather than seeing it means taking its sound

blocks.note: a whine is a peevish complaint

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen to a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks 22 down, hock, as an example: hock is a German white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine, one example of the drink.

clue.text: Antioxidant element central to booziest brunches

indicators.note: what is central to a word lies at its middle, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the two middle letters of the first word
the two middle letters of the second word

explanation.surface: A health claim about a mineral that matters most at heavy-drinking brunches.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element and a trace nutrient that protects cells against oxidative damage.

clue.text: Avarice, accepting n divided by 23 for agricultural payment rate

indicators.note: a word that accepts something takes it inside
a word divided by something is split open with that thing sitting inside it

blocks.note: avarice is greed
n is the grammar abbreviation for noun
the answer to 23 across, whose chess abbreviation is P

explanation.surface: Reads like a maths formula for farm subsidies: greed with n over a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the pawn's letter splits the grammar word, and that whole chunk goes inside the avarice word. In chess notation P stands for pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The green pound was the special exchange rate used to convert EU farm support prices into sterling.
